headline: Venstre sinks to 5.8 per cent, its lowest poll ever
deck: Five of the liberal party's MPs voted against its line on a fertiliser law, and one says he may do so again.
standard: Venstre, a liberal party, stands at 5.8 per cent in a poll by Epinion, a polling firm, for DR published on Thursday. The party has never polled lower.

Five of its MPs, Søren Gade among them, voted against the party line on a law tightening farmers' use of fertiliser. On Tuesday Gade said he might again vote 'by his own conviction' on a proposed national pesticide ban.

Søs Marie Serup, the party's former press chief, blames conflicts over farming and climate that built up over a long time, not Troels Lund Poulsen, the party leader. 'This term will be like walking through hell,' she told Kristeligt Dagblad.
short: Venstre, a liberal party, stands at 5.8 per cent in a poll by Epinion, a polling firm, for DR, its lowest ever. Five of its MPs voted against the party line on a fertiliser law.
